events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.78)
events.body:
NS-0 routes this case: the trip was cancelled by the driver with a rider no-show allegation, so the $6.61 fee stands only if NS-1 is met [F4][NS-0].

NS-1 (i): the platform shows the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:07:40 [F6][NS-1]. NS-1 (ii): at that moment the GPS placed him 181 m from the pickup point, inside the 200 m arrival radius, and his closest approach was 60 m [F6][F1][NS-1]. NS-1 (iii): he then stayed continuously within the radius for 220 s (3 min 40 s) and was stationary from 14:07:20 to 14:11:20 (4 min 0 s), i.e. well past the 3:01 threshold, before cancelling at 14:11:20 [F6][F3][F4][NS-1]. what_would_change: Had the driver tapped I'm Here more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: This is a driver cancellation with a rider no-show allegation, so the $6.61 fee is only valid if NS-1's three requirements (I'm Here tap, GPS inside the pickup point at the tap, and over 3 minutes waited there) are all met.
The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:07:40 while he was 181 m from the pickup point, which shows he was not at the pick-up location according to GPS data when he indicated arrival.

Although the driver stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap and the record shows 4 min 40 s cumulative within 200 m, his stationary position from 14:07:20 to 14:11:20 was 181 m from the pin — a distance the rider could not see from the entrance, consistent with the rider's message "I'm at the entrance, I don't see you" at 14:09.

The rider's complaint that the driver was not at the entrance where the pin was is corroborated by the system GPS record of 181 m, which outweighs the driver's post-trip written statement that he was "at the pickup, a short walk from the entrance".
Because NS-1's requirement that the driver be at the pick-up location according to GPS at the time of the "I'm Here" tap is not satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full.

The driver's own account and the two upheld no-show disputes against him in the last 90 days (2 of 2 upheld) support referring his account to Ryde for review under the abuse-of-cancellation/waiting-fee-button rule.

weaknesses: F5 and F2 show the platform recorded arrival at 14:06:40 and 4 min 40 s cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation, and F6 shows 3 min 40 s inside 200 m after the tap — the driver will argue the >3-minute wait condition of NS-1(iii) is met on the system record.

F1 shows the driver's closest approach was only 60 m from the pickup at 14:07:00, so the driver will argue he was effectively at the pickup point and that the 181 m stationary reading is map noise versus the 60 m approach.

The rider's own message F10 is the only chat evidence the rider could not find the driver; there is no message showing the rider asked him to move or that the rider was waiting at a different entrance.

F17 shows the rider has 1 dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld, so the rider's own dispute record gives the driver a rhetorical counterweight despite F18 showing the driver has 2 of 2 no-show disputes upheld.

claims.assertion: The driver did everything NS-1 requires: he pressed "I'm Here" at 14:07:40 while inside the pickup zone and the GPS record shows he then stayed within 200 m of the pickup point for the remaining 3 min 40 s of the wait.

The three NS-1(ii)/(iii) conditions are independently corroborated: the driver was first within 200 m at 14:06:40 (F2), his closest approach to the pin was 60 m at 14:07:00 (F1), and he accumulated 4 min 40 s inside the 200 m zone before cancelling — well past the 3:01 threshold.

The wait itself is documented: the driver was stationary from 14:07:20 to 14:11:20 at (1.2921, 103.8471), 181 m from the pickup point, a 4-minute wait that satisfies the >3-minute requirement of NS-1(iii).

The in-app chat is complete (3 messages, all timestamped) and shows the driver informing the rider of his exact position at 14:07 ("I'm here … at the side road") before waiting another 4 minutes and only then cancelling at 14:11:20.

The rider's complaint that "the driver was not at the entrance where the pin was" is not disputed as a matter of physics — 60 m is the closest approach on record — but it is not the test: NS-1(ii) requires the driver to be within the pickup zone, and the system records show he was within 200 m continuously for 4 min 40 s, so the cancellation fee stands and no refund is due.

The rider's own message confirms she was waiting but did not come the short distance to the side road, and the platform recorded the driver's arrival at 14:06:40 with cancellation 4 min 40 s later — i.e. a genuine no-show within the terms of A1, not an abusive cancellation.

This is not a driver-side cancellation without cause: the record shows arrival, the "I'm Here" tap, a stationary wait and a rider no-show, so NS-3 (which would require a full $6.61 refund) and NS-2 (which applies only where an NS-1 condition fails) are both inapplicable; the correct outcome is no_action.

There is no safety dimension to this dispute: no message, statement or allegation in the file reads as a threat, harassment or dangerous driving, and the weather was fair — so SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation is not warranted.

weaknesses: The rider's own message (F10: "I'm at the entrance, I don't see you") and the 181 m recorded stationary position (F3) show the driver was not at the pin, which supports the rider's framing though not the NS-1(ii) test (F2 shows he was inside the 200 m pickup zone the whole time).

The driver's written statement adds a fact the system records do not support: he says he "parked at the pickup" while GPS places his stationary position 181 m from the pin and his closest approach at 60 m (F1, F3) — that overstatement invites the judge to discount his account and can be contrasted with the "side road" wording in his own chat message (F9).

The driver's profile shows 2 no-show disputes upheld in 90 days (F18), so under RD-6-style reasoning a flag_account adjunct is plausible even though NS-1 is satisfied; the fee dispute itself remains no_action.

NS-7 gives Ryde absolute discretion over refunds and NS-2's rider-side remedy is the RydeHELP appeal, so a sympathetic reading of the rider's "not at the entrance" complaint could still result in a goodwill voucher on manual review (F7).

points.response: D1 misstates the test: NS-1(ii) requires the driver to be at the pick-up location according to GPS when he taps "I'm Here", and F6 places the tap at 181 m from the pickup point, not at it; staying within 200 m afterwards cannot retro-fit the tap.

A 60 m closest approach at 14:07:00 (F1) is not the pickup point either, and the 4 min 40 s inside the 200 m zone (F2) is a data-layer measuring radius, not the pin the rider was told to meet; NS-1 requires presence at the pick-up location, which the record never shows.

D3 concedes the decisive point: the stationary wait ran from 14:07:20 to 14:11:20 at 181 m from the pickup point (F3), i.e. the driver spent the whole qualifying wait away from the pin his own message described as "the side road".

D4 actually helps the rider: the driver's own 14:07 message says he was "at the side road" (F9), which is not the entrance/pin, and the rider's reply at 14:09 (F10) shows she was at the pin and could not find him while he still had ~2 more minutes to move.

D5 asks the judge to substitute the 200 m measuring radius for the pick-up location in NS-1(ii); on the system's own records the driver was 181 m from the pin at the tap (F6) and stationary at 181 m during the wait (F3), so a NS-1 condition fails and NS-2 mandates a full $6.61 refund.

F10 shows the opposite of a no-show: the rider was present at the entrance and actively messaging at 14:09, so her failure to find a car parked 181 m away at a side road not visible from the pin (F3, F9) cannot be charged to her.
D7 fails because NS-1 is not satisfied: the tap came at 181 m from the pickup (F6) and the wait was spent at 181 m (F3), so NS-2 applies and no_action is not available.
The rider does not seek SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation and agrees there is no safety dimension; this point is irrelevant to the fee.

C3 is narrowed: the rider relies on the 181 m stationary position at the tap and during the wait (F6, F3) rather than on cumulative time inside 200 m (F2), which the driver correctly cites against her.

C6 is maintained but only as an adjunct: the driver's station 181 m from the pin while pressing "I'm Here" (F6, F3) plus 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F18) support sending his account to Ryde for review, while the fee finding rests on NS-2 alone.

Accepted as a statement of the test — and it is met: F6 shows the "I'm Here" tap at 14:07:40 with a continuous 3 min 40 s inside 200 m thereafter, F2 shows 4 min 40 s cumulative within 200 m before cancellation, and F3 shows the 4-minute stationary wait, so all three NS-1 conditions hold.

The 181 m figure (F6) is still inside the pickup zone on the system record — NS-1(ii) asks whether GPS shows the driver at the pick-up location within the 200 m data-layer radius, and F2 proves he was inside that radius from 14:06:40 and stayed inside it for the whole wait; the rider's advocate offers no clause requiring pin-point accuracy.

Visibility is not the test in NS-1; the test is the GPS record, and F1 shows the driver's closest approach was 60 m at 14:07:00 while his 181 m stationary position (F3) is a single coordinate that still lies within the 200 m radius (F2) — non-satisfaction under NS-2 is therefore not established.

Conceded in part: the driver's post-trip statement that he was "at the pickup" is overstated against F1/F3, and the system record wins over statements; but the only record that matters for NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) is F2/F6, which shows compliance, so the overstatement does not defeat the fee.

NS-2 is not triggered because none of the NS-1 conditions failed as a matter of system record (F6: tap inside the zone; F2: 4 min 40 s inside 200 m; F3: 4-minute stationary wait), so refund_full of $6.61 is not the correct outcome — no_action is.

Profile facts cannot decide the case and the rider's brief itself concedes the NS-1 conditions on the system record (their own weaknesses list F5/F2/F6); a flag_account adjunct under RD-6 requires the underlying violation to be established, which it is not here.
